title: Google finally releases Gemini 4 Argon
summary:
After months sitting on the sidelines of the frontier AI race, Google has finally launched its long-awaited Gemini 4 Argon model, claiming it can compete with the best the industry has to offer.
Google says Argon delivers “frontier reasoning and improved performance across complex workflows,” while cutting down on hedging, repetition, and the cliches that continue to plague AI chatbots.
The launch fills in some of the blanks left behind from when Google first teased Argon a few weeks ago.
In line with other recent frontier model releases, the public rollout follows a limited release to a select set of “trusted cyber defenders” to be tested for potential risks.
But Argon’s arrival suggests we can’t count Google out of the AI race just yet.

title: Character.AI files for bankruptcy
summary:
Character.AI, one of the first breakout startups of the generative AI boom, has filed for bankruptcy and is selling some of its assets to Disney.
In a press release and blog post published Monday, Character said it had filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US to facilitate the sale of the company and its assets.
In its bankruptcy filing, Character listed estimated liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.
As part of the proposed sale, Disney would serve as the lead bidder for Character.AI’s assets, setting a baseline for competing offers.
“As we navigate this process, maintaining a safe and engaging experience for our community remains a top priority,” it said.

summary:
